facts.statement: The type species T. dissipata was discovered near the village of Céreste-en-Luberon in France.
facts.quote: The type species, T. dissipata, was found near the village of Céreste-en-Luberon in France.

facts.statement: A second species, T. oechslerorum, was described from a nearly complete skeleton found south of Wiesloch, Germany.
facts.quote: A second species, T. oechslerorum, was described based on a nearly complete and slightly dissociated skeleton found south of Wiesloch, Germany.

facts.statement: Mayr described the type species in 2000 based on a strongly dissociated skeleton from Rupelian deposits near Céreste-en-Luberon, southern France.
facts.quote: The type species was described by Mayr (2000) after a strongly dissociated skeleton preserving vertebrae, ribs, humeri, coracoids, scapulae, furcula, pelvis and the legs from Rupelian aged deposits near Céreste-en-Luberon village, southern France.

facts.statement: Mayr and Knopf named T. oechslerorum in 2007 based on an almost complete skeleton missing only the head and right foot.
facts.quote: In 2007, Mayr and Knopf named a second species, T. oechslerorum after an almost complete slightly dissociated skeleton that only lacks the head and the right foot.

facts.statement: The species name T. oechslerorum honors Annette and Harald Oechsler for their contribution to finding the fossils.
facts.quote: The species name honors Annette and Harald Oechsler, who significantly contributed to the discovery of the Frauenweiler fossils.

facts.statement: Turnipax is an extinct genus of buttonquail that lived during the Oligocene Rupelian epoch.
facts.quote: Turnipax is an extinct genus of buttonquail from the Oligocene Rupelian epoch.

facts.statement: The genus name Turnipax combines parts of the names of the charadriiform genus Scolopax and the turnicid genus Turnix.
facts.quote: The genus name is a combination of Scolopax, a genus of charadriiform and Turnix, a genus of turnicid.

facts.statement: The family Turnipacidae was originally established to include T. dissipata and the bird species Cerestenia pulchrapenna.
facts.quote: The new family Turnipacidae was originally created for T. dissipata and tentatively Cerestenia pulchrapenna, another bird species from Céreste.

facts.statement: The family Turnipacidae was originally classified within the order Charadriiformes.
facts.quote: This family was placed within Charadriiformes.

facts.statement: Mayr and Knopf (2007) proposed that Turnipax represents a stem lineage of the family Turnicidae.
facts.quote: Mayr and Knopf (2007) stated that Turnipax was a stem-lineage representative of Turnicidae.

facts.statement: Later studies classified Cerestenia as a stem Turnicidae, similar to Turnipax.
facts.quote: Later studies included Cerestenia as a stem Turnicidae, just as Turnipax.

facts.statement: Turnipax lived during the Rupelian epoch of the Oligocene.
facts.quote: Turnipax is an extinct genus of buttonquail from the Oligocene Rupelian epoch.

facts.statement: Turnipax lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Rupelian (33.9 to 27.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The presence of gastroliths in T. oechslerorum suggests it had at least a facultatively granivorous diet.
facts.quote: The holotype of T. oechslerorum preserves several gastroliths. This suggests at least a facultatively granivorous diet.

facts.statement: Modern buttonquails are omnivorous, feeding on seeds, plant matter, and invertebrates while ingesting grit to aid digestion.
facts.quote: Modern buttonquails are omnivorous; they feed on various seeds, plant matter and invertebrates. They also ingest grit and small pebbles to aid digestion.

facts.statement: The Frauenweiler fossil site where T. oechslerorum was found represents marine deposits within a clay pit.
facts.quote: The Frauenweiler fossil site, part of the Rauenberg Lagerstätte, is a clay pit that represents marine deposits.

facts.statement: The marine deposits at the Frauenweiler site were likely formed during a transgression caused by rifting activities.
facts.quote: These were likely deposited during a transgression caused by rifting activities.

facts.statement: The Rauenberg Lagerstätte is similar to the Oligocene Luberon area where T. dissipata was discovered.
facts.quote: The Rauenberg Lagerstätte is similar to the Oligocene Luberon area where T. dissipata was found.
